title: Delta eval orchestration for config/model variant matrices and prompt cohorts
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Objective: Implement an orchestration layer that automatically runs focused evals when model binaries, runtime config (batching/quantization/kernel profile), or prompt set changes are proposed. Instead of full-corpus regressions for every change, we will compute a delta evaluation plan scoped to affected prompt cohorts and model/config variant intersections. The system should: 1) subscribe to config and model change events (CI, runtime config service, and model registry), 2) compute minimal but high-confidence eval subsets via prompt-cohort coverage and sensitivity heuristics, 3) run parallelized regression jobs with per-variant baselines, and 4) expose results to the Console with actionable gating rules (block rollout, require steward signoff, or auto-roll back). This ticket covers the orchestration, cohort selection heuristics, and the RBAC/ownership workflow for golden prompt cohorts.
acceptance_criteria: A config change hook exists that can be wired into CI and runtime change stream (proof: test webhook + sample event)
Delta planner computes eval plans that are <30% of full-corpus size for typical model/kernel tweaks and covers >= 90% of expected behavioral impact (measured via simulated perturbation trials)
Evals run on dedicated 'delta' workers and produce per-prompt and per-cohort metrics that the Console can visualize (latency, pass/fail, regression delta)
Gating rules can be expressed and enforceable: block rollout, require steward approval, or schedule extended regression (links to configuration DSL examples)
Prompt cohort ownership metadata and ACLs are stored and enforced; changes to golden cohorts require an authorized steward signature (audit trail visible in Console)
End-to-end demo: trigger from a PR that modifies quantization config and show the delta eval run, Console alert, and an automated canary hold
updates: 2025-11-10 - Kickoff: scoped work with PM and Design. Decided to focus on 'cohort-first' planner rather than naive sample-based sampling to improve signal-to-noise for small changes. Milestone: prototype planner in 2 weeks.

2025-11-17 - Prototype: basic planner written (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-orch PR #234). Planner reads change event and returns affected prompt cohort list using prompt tags and model-capability fingerprints. Ran local smoke evals against runtime-1.20 baseline.

2025-11-21 - Trade-off discussion: storage of golden cohorts. Options considered: immutable signed snapshots in CAS vs. managed versioned collections with soft-deletes. We chose CAS for binary integrity and faster bisection; steward metadata stored separately for ACLs and human-readable provenance.

2025-11-25 - Integration: wired planner to CI change stream (proof event) and kicked off delta eval jobs on delta-workers pool. Observed 12x speedup vs full-corpus for kernel micro-tuning change, with clear per-cohort deltas shown in Grafana panel (dashboard link below).

2025-11-28 - RBAC: added basic steward role enforcement to cohort edit flow. Implemented audit log entries that reference KMS-signed acceptance tokens for golden cohort updates. UX team to add steward signoff CTA in Console (DES ticket referenced).

2025-12-02 - In Review: documentation PR opened (confluence + repo README). PM requested runbook for false positives and recommended fallback to full regression when delta signal is weak. Preparing demo for stakeholder review on 2025-12-08.
